title: Starter Mentorship Rotations & Evidence Journal
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight, mentor-forward rotation plan + evidence journal designed to accelerate practical impact for product/engineering new hires during their first 6 weeks. The doc is intentionally checklist-y and evidence-oriented so managers can make consistent, fast decisions about role fit and next steps without a long audit.

Intended audience:
- New hire (IC) and assigned mentor
- Hiring manager and People Ops partner
- Onboarding buddy pool

How to use this doc (quick):
1) Mentor and new hire read together on day 0 and pick 2 rotation themes (codebase, infra, product-scope, customer-support).
2) Each week, the new hire completes 3 small, observable artifacts (tiny PR, runbook note, customer repro steps, design doc sketch). Mentor logs a short evidence blurb and a 1–3 sentence rating.
3) At the end of week 3 and week 6, manager + mentor use the rubric section to decide if extra support, role adjustment, or celebration is needed.

Weeks & rotation prompts (pick 2 themes total; rotate focus each week):
- Week 0 (prep): account access, repo walkthrough, dev environment: confirm: local dev build runs, test suite subset passes, slack channels joined.
- Week 1 (surface-level): find a small bug or doc gap and open a PR. Evidence: PR link + brief note on learning.
- Week 2 (ownership micro): ship a small feature flag toggle or alert tweak. Evidence: changelog + deployment note.
- Week 3 (cross-team): shadow support or product triage for 1 hour; write a short post-mortem of one customer issue. Evidence: post-mortem doc link.
- Week 4 (scale/infra): add monitoring or a pipeline test; write a runbook short. Evidence: monitoring dashboard screenshot + runbook blurb.
- Week 5 (quality & eval): propose a test/refactor and land it; write a short rationale. Evidence: PR link + before/after perf or error metrics.
- Week 6 (handoff & plan): present a 10-min demo + propose a 30–60 day plan for impact. Evidence: slide notes + manager summary.

Artifact examples (3 per week, concrete):
- Tiny PR (<200 LOC) that fixes a bug or improves test coverage (link).
- One-sheeter: "How the feature works" for another pod to onboard them (doc link).
- Runbook stub covering one common alert and the first 3 triage steps (screenshot/text).
- Customer repro steps + observed logs (paste snippet).
- Short unit/integration test demonstrating an edge case (test name + link).

Mentor responsibilities (concise):
- Day 0: 30–45m orientation: map out access, local setup risks, short reading list (3 docs).
- Weekly: 30m touchpoint to unblock, review artifacts, and add evidence notes below.
- Midpoint (end w3): 30m calibration with manager to surface any gaps.
- Final (w6): 45m demo + signals discussion; decide follow-up actions.

Evidence log template (mentor fills):
- Week #: [1..6]
- Artifact title (link):
- What I saw (1–2 sentences):
- Signal (positive / caution / blocking):
- Suggested next step (mentor):

Example entry (realistic):
- Week 2
- Artifact: "fix/alert-threshold-typo" PR #412 (link)
- What I saw: new hire located coupling in alert code, suggested narrower scope and added test; PR had clear commit messages.
- Signal: positive
- Suggested next step: pair on a slightly larger incident-runbook next week.

Quick interview-rubric snippets (use these during final w6 calibration):
Scoring: 3 = meets expectations, 2 = partial, 1 = needs work. Use combined mentorship evidence + code artifacts.
- Codebase literacy: 3 = edits across multiple modules with tests; 2 = single module + tests; 1 = needs help navigating repos.
- Problem decomposition: 3 = breaks a vague request into 2–3 small deliverables; 2 = needs guidance to scope; 1 = unclear deliverable.
- Ownership & follow-through: 3 = closes tickets, writes runbooks, communicates blockers; 2 = closed with prompting; 1 = delayed/can't finish.
- Cross-team communication: 3 = concise docs and effective async updates; 2 = requires edits; 1 = poor handoffs.
- Quality & testing mindset: 3 = adds tests and verifies deploy behavior; 2 = adds some tests; 1 = no tests/unsafe deploys.

Manager checklist (for w3 and w6 calibration):
- Have we observed at least 9 artifacts total by w3 and 18 by w6? (goal: ~3/wk)
- Does the evidence show increasing independence?
- Are there consistent blockers in access, tooling, or product clarity?
- Is mentorship bandwidth sufficient for the next 30 days?
- Recommendation: continue with current plan | add focused remediation | adjust role scope | expedite leveling conversation

Hiring-plan alignment notes (how this ties back to hiring signals):
- For roles hired for "fast-embedded impact," expect 6-week demonstrable code + one cross-team artifact.
- For "long-term research" hires, swap code artifacts for design write-ups, literature notes, and experiments.
- Use rubric scores (aggregate average) to inform leveling & comp discussions at 45–60 days.

Manager & mentor tips (short):
- Keep evidence short: 1–3 lines plus a link. The goal is visible signal, not long prose.
- Focus on next-best-step actions. Ask: "what one thing would make them 2x more effective this week?"
- Avoid conflating onboarding tasks (access) with competence signals. Fix access issues immediately but mark them separately.

Notes to self / unresolved questions (working):
- Q: How to consistently track non-code hires' artifacts? Add role templates (PM, design, SRE) next iteration.
- Q: Do we need a lightweight scoring UI? Right now this is manual in Drive; consider small Airtable tracker.
- TODO: create role-specific artifact templates and add to Confluence onboarding library.

Appendix: short templates to paste into mentor notes (one-liners)
- "Week {n}: reviewed {artifact}. Strengths: {short}. Risk: {short}. Next: {short}."
- "Calibrated with manager: {decision} — next checkpoint {date}."

End — keep this doc deliberately short and iterated. If it proves useful, we can convert into a sheet with links and auto-counting of artifacts for quicker manager reviews.

[Author note] Aisha P. — created this after a dozen messy onboarding retros at product and infra pods; designed to reduce ambiguous "couldn't ramp" calls by turning them into observable artifacts.
